clue.text: Bishop is OK about getting hard on, though it means utter ruin

indicators.note: about here means turned around and mixed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A bishop excited despite the risk of disgrace, typical Private Eye innuendo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges B, IS and OK into KIBOS, then 'getting hard on' adds H at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is to finish it off completely, to ruin it.

clue.text: One mad frolic on one date with La Bollard's original pair, …

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one

indicators.note: to frolic is to caper about, so the letters of mad are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
Private Eye's name for the editor Eve Pollard, so her first name

explanation.surface: A wild night out on a date with the Eye's 'La Bollard', running into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolic' rearranges MAD into DAM. Eve Pollard, editor and wife of Sir Nick Lloyd, was mocked as 'La Bollard' in Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Adam and Eve were the first man and woman, the first couple of humanity.

clue.text: … model held by Sir Nick!

indicators.note: held by means the letter for model sits inside the word Sir

parts.note: taken as written
the Model T was the classic Ford car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: Eve Pollard, a model, in the arms of her husband Sir Nick Lloyd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' puts T inside SIR. 'Sir Nick' looks like a name, but the definition is 'Nick' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick and stir are both slang for prison.

clue.text: An unconventional atrocity?

parts.note: unconventional reads as breaking the Geneva Conventions, the treaties on the conduct of war

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconventional' suggests merely unusual, but here it means in breach of the Conventions that govern war.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocities such as killing prisoners violate the Geneva Conventions, and that is what makes them criminal acts of war.

clue.text: One way to get dole money is in pumping iron

definitions.text: One way to get dole money

indicators.note: is in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters are found across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that the unemployed can earn benefit at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemployment benefit in Britain was once paid by giro, a cheque sent through the post-office banking system.

clue.text: No oscar — is devastated, resulting in a stupor

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
oscar without its O: 'No oscar' says lose the O, the letter oscar stands for in the NATO alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film star denied an Oscar is crushed and sinks into a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No oscar' does double duty: NO is fodder, and it also says oscar loses its O, leaving SCAR. 'devastated' rearranges NO, SCAR and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a state of drowsiness or unconsciousness caused by drugs, a stupor.

clue.text: Crown belittled as a result of Diana's first media outing?

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of Diana's

parts.note: the first letter of Diana's

indicators.note: an outing takes the word media out of its usual form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's first television interview is said to have diminished the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes D from Diana's, and 'outing' rearranges MEDIA into IADEM. 'belittled as a result of' is surface padding linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A diadem is a jewelled headband worn as a symbol of royalty, a kind of crown.

clue.text: Not my version of the old soldier

indicators.note: a version of something is a different form of it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone disowning a particular account of an old soldier's story.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty was the nickname of Field Marshal Montgomery, the British Second World War commander.

clue.text: Ethnic habit assimilated by backward one-time royal partner

indicators.note: something assimilated is taken into a larger body, so these letters go inside the others
backward tells us to read the letters for one and time from right to left

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a sari is the traditional garment of Indian women; habit here means clothing

explanation.surface: An exotic costume adopted by a dim former royal consort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time' looks like 'former' but splits into two pieces; 'backward' turns them into TNA, and 'assimilated by' puts the Indian garment inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian emperor, so the consort or partner of a royal ruler.

clue.text: It's pointless the House going to Brenda — not her type at all

indicators.note: pointless means without a compass point, so the point S is dropped

parts.note: the House of Commons, the lower chamber of the UK Parliament
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, whose royal cipher is ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A jibe at Parliament handing matters to the Queen, who would never mix with such people.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen 'Brenda'; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina. Removing S, a compass point, leaves COMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: A commoner is anyone without noble or royal rank, the opposite social class to the Queen.

clue.text: About blight — check genital area!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
rot is decay or blight in plants
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A doctor's warning to examine the private parts for a fungal disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The crotch is the part of the body where the legs meet, around the groin.

clue.text: Not what he seems, Portillo at first, dear

indicators.note: at first means take only the opening letter of Portillo

parts.note: the first letter of Portillo, Michael Portillo being a Conservative cabinet minister of the 1990s
honey is a term of endearment, like dear

explanation.surface: A dig at the Tory minister Michael Portillo as a fake, with a mock-affectionate 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone phoney is a fraud or impostor, pretending to be something they are not.

clue.text: A vintage upmarket ride, Di?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Austin and Vanden Plas ..., a luxury British car of past decades

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks whether Diana is a vintage ride; the two halves are separate meanings, an old luxury car and Diana's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Princess was a British luxury car model, and Diana held the royal title Princess of Wales.

clue.text: Tumescent in short pants

definitions.meaning: first meaning: swollen or puffed up
second meaning: breathing in short puffs, short-winded

explanation.walkthrough: 'Short pants' suggests a boy's trousers, but pants here are gasps: something coming in puffs is a second sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen tissue is described this way, and the same adjective means short of breath or blowing in gusts.

clue.text: Subjects nationally should have greater moral emphasis we're now told

definitions.text: Subjects nationally should have greater moral emphasis we're now told

parts.words: Subjects nationally should have greater moral emphasis we're now told
parts.note: a topical news line: the official advice of the mid-1990s that schools' set syllabus should teach more morality

explanation.walkthrough: 'Subjects' suggests citizens of the realm, but it means school subjects, and the national set of them is the course of study laid down for England's schools.
explanation.definitionFit: England's National Curriculum fixes the school subjects taught across the country; in 1996 its overseers urged more moral teaching.

clue.text: Tartish character a mother of two would become

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... in the nursery rhyme, who made some tarts

definitions.text: a mother of two would become
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Diana, mother of two princes, said she wanted to be a queen of people's hearts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tartish' suggests a loose woman but here means connected with tarts, the pastries in the rhyme. In her 1995 Panorama interview Diana said she would like to be a queen in people's hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: The card and nursery-rhyme figure is the tart-baker, and the phrase is the title Diana claimed for herself.

clue.text: Who on the continent gets to toss the collaborator?

parts.note: qui is French for who
to sling is to throw or toss

explanation.surface: Asking which European gets to throw out a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidkun Quisling led Norway's Nazi puppet government, and his name came to mean any traitor who works with an occupier.

clue.text: One who squeals about love has kinky, crafty accommodation for couples

indicators.note: about means the informer's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a nark is a police informer, one who squeals
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of has are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An informer exposing a kinky hotel for couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' turns 'has' into AHS, and 'about' wraps the informer around love and AHS. 'Crafty' means in the form of a craft, a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is the vessel that carried the animals two by two, so a boat holding pairs.

clue.text: Ability to read french article about sex — spicy!

indicators.note: about means the article goes around the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
it is a coy slang word for sex
racy means lively and slightly risque, like spicy

explanation.surface: A literate person reading something saucy in French about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the skill of reading and writing.

clue.text: Come to a sticky end?

parts.note: the idiom for dying badly is reread as a crude joke about sexual release

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'come' and 'sticky end' describe orgasm, Private Eye's schoolboy humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the peak of sexual pleasure, the point at which a man comes.

clue.text: Insinuate he's an OBN candidate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to edge your way into favour
second meaning: a sycophant, fit for Private Eye's mock award, the Order of the Brown Nose

explanation.walkthrough: The OBN, Order of the Brown Nose, is Private Eye's joke honour for grovelling flatterers.
explanation.definitionFit: A creep is a fawning flatterer, and to creep is to work your way in by stealth.

clue.text: Carling's first affair (female abandoned) rocked the land

indicators.note: rocked means shaken up, so these letters are reordered
first means take only the opening letter of Carling's

parts.note: the first letter of Carling's; Will Carling, England rugby captain, was linked with Diana

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter for female is dropped from affair

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Will Carling's rumoured affair with Diana scandalised the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes C from Carling's; 'abandoned' drops one F (female) from AFFAIR, leaving AFAIR; 'rocked' rearranges C and AFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is a continent, a land mass.

clue.text: Grass causes bloke to be beset by form of BSE

indicators.note: something beset by others is surrounded by them, so these letters go inside
a form of something is a version of it, so these letters are reworked into another order

parts.note: taken as written: bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease
lad is an informal word for a man, like bloke

explanation.surface: Eating grass gives a man mad cow disease, a joke from the 1990s BSE scare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' gives BES, and 'to be beset by' puts the bloke inside it. 'Grass' looks like a verb (to inform) but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades are the individual leaves of grass, so the plural stands for grass in general.

clue.text: A big supporter of Bristol City?

definitions.text: A big supporter of Bristol City?

parts.words: A big supporter of Bristol City?
parts.note: reads as a football fan, but Bristol City is rhyming slang for a breast and the supporter is a bra

explanation.walkthrough: Bristol City is a football club, but in rhyming slang 'Bristol City' means titty, so 'Bristols' are breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bra cup size holds a big bust, so it supports the bosom.

clue.text: Just a game, housing to Major

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a board game, a form of draughts
second meaning: the country house of the British prime minister, John Major at the time

explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the prime minister's official country residence in Buckinghamshire; John Major was PM when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game played on a checked board shares its name with the prime minister's country home.

clue.text: Labour's leader (prune) goes about with devoted following

indicators.note: goes about means the word for prune surrounds the letter

parts.note: to cut is to prune

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of Labour's

parts.note: the first letter of Labour's

explanation.surface: Tony Blair trimming his party while surrounded by loyal followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult is a group with devotion to a person or cause, an adoring band of followers.

clue.text: Colourless Gingrich, it's said, right next in line to Clinton

indicators.note: it's said means we take the sound of the US politician's first name

parts.note: Newt Gingrich, Republican Speaker of the US House in the 1990s
Al Gore was Bill Clinton's vice-president, first in succession

explanation.surface: Calling Newt Gingrich dull, and wrongly placing him behind Clinton in the succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' turns NEWT into the sound NEUT. The surface suggests Gingrich is next in line, but AL comes from Al Gore, Clinton's vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral describes a colour such as grey or beige that lacks strong hue.

clue.text: Defunct organ, one located inside beer belly

indicators.note: located inside says the letter for one is placed within the magazine's name

parts.note: Punch, the British humorous magazine, which closed in 1992; an organ is a publication
a is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Talk of an obsolete body part inside a drinker's gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defunct organ' points to anatomy, but an organ is also a periodical: Punch, a long-running British humour magazine that had just closed. 'located inside' puts A within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch is a large protruding stomach, the kind blamed on drinking beer.
